target.title: Bound QA runtime parity mock request reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA runtime-parity reads `${mockBaseUrl}/debug/requests` from a local mock server and previously used `response.json()` directly. That endpoint should return a small request snapshot array, but a broken mock server could return a large successful body and make the QA process buffer it before any validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the unbounded `response.json()` call with the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper using a 256 KiB cap and a 30s idle timeout. The existing fail-closed behavior is preserved: non-OK, malformed, oversized, or stalled mock responses are caught by `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` and treated as missing mock tool-call data.

## User Impact

QA runtime-parity remains tolerant of unavailable or malformed mock debug data, but successful mock responses are now bounded before JSON parsing. Valid mock request arrays still resolve tool-call order normally.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): strip trailing assistant messages after sessions_yield artifact removal
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109638.

After `sessions_yield`, `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` removes aborted assistant messages and yield interrupt custom messages, but leaves trailing regular assistant messages (from pre-yield tool work) intact. When a sub-agent completes and auto-announce tries to inject a continuation message, it fails because the last visible message is an assistant — causing a deadlock.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.sessions-yield.ts`**: Added a second while-loop pass in `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` that strips any trailing regular assistant messages remaining after the yield-specific artifacts are removed. Updated `removeTrailingEntries` predicate to match.
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`**: Added regression test verifying that after stripping a transcript with pre-yield tool work, the last message is a `tool_result` (not an assistant).

## Why this is safe

`stripSessionsYieldArtifacts` is only called inside the yield abort handler (after `waitForSessionsYieldAbortSettle`). It never runs on non-yield sessions. Trailing assistant messages in the yield context are always intermediate tool-calling work — not meaningful final responses.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: After sessions_yield, auto-announce continuation delivery fails with role-continuity error because trailing assistant messages block injection.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.18.0, vitest

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts -t "trailing assistant" --reporter=verbose`

**Evidence after fix**: Test passes in both shards (agents-core 55ms, agents-embedded-agent 43ms). Last message after stripping is confirmed to be tool_result role.

**Observed result after fix**: 2 test files passed, 2 tests passed, 8 skipped (non-matching filter).

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end yield→announce flow (requires live sub-agent spawn + completion cycle, covered by integration environment).

target.title: fix(codex): continue after optional input timeout
target.body:
Related: #109724

AI-assisted: Codex was used to implement and review this change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Codex through the app-server integration could see an optional input question keep the turn waiting for a human answer or a broader run timeout, even when Codex supplied an automatic-resolution window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The user-input bridge now preserves the optional app-server deadline, returns an empty answer set when that exact window expires, and clears the timer through the existing request cleanup path after a human answer, abort, replacement request, or server-side resolution.

The implementation follows the current upstream Codex contract at `openai/codex@315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304`: [`autoResolutionMs` is the optional client auto-resolution window](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs#L71-L77), [Codex bounds it before dispatch](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs#L123-L133), and [app-server forwards the value to its client](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L703-L746). [The TUI's fixed countdown is an explicitly client-specific policy](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/315195492c80fdade38e917c18f9584efd599304/codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/request_user_input/mod.rs#L281-L300), so OpenClaw honors the app-server wire value instead of copying that policy.

The branch also updates the Codex binding test fixture for the `features.goals: false` entry introduced by #109724. This is a test-only baseline correction; it does not change runtime configuration.

## User Impact

Optional Codex questions can now release the waiting turn automatically at the requested deadline. Human answers still win when submitted in time, and completed or replaced requests leave no stale timer that can affect a later question.

## Evidence

- Real Codex app-server 0.144.1 behavior proof over stdio, using the production client and bridge with a real 60-second clock (no mocked transport or fake timers):

target.title: feat(plugins): tool-name matchers scope tool hooks and Codex native hook relay spawns
target.body:
Closes #109522

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where every Codex app-server tool call spawns a full `openclaw hooks relay` node process (~300–400 MB) once any `before_tool_call` hook, trusted tool policy, or codex tool-result middleware is registered — even when that registration only targets a single tool (e.g. the `message` tool). This is the relay fan-out tracked in #91009 / #107641 (kernel OOMs, dozens of concurrent relay processes on small hosts). The spawn gate was a global boolean, so no registration surface could express "only these tools".

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an optional `matcher` (exact tool-name list) to the three tool-scoped registration surfaces — `api.on("before_tool_call"/"after_tool_call", handler, { matcher })`, `registerTrustedToolPolicy({ matcher })`, and `registerAgentToolResultMiddleware(handler, { matcher })`. Dispatch skips scoped registrations for non-matching tools, and the Codex adapter forwards the union of registered matchers as the installed `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` hook matcher (pipe-joined exact names), so Codex returns before spawning any relay process for uncovered tools (verified against the pinned harness `rust-v0.144.5`: `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/common.rs` exact-matcher semantics, `events/pre_tool_use.rs` early return).

Key boundaries:
- **Omitted matcher = match-all everywhere**; existing plugins are unaffected, and a match-all union emits byte-identical Codex hook config, preserving existing session trust hashes (matcher key stays omitted, not null).
- **Fail-closed preserved**: any unscoped registration, an active native loop detector, an oversized union, or a name Codex would treat as regex source (anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` — an invalid pattern would silently disable the hook upstream) falls back to match-all. The `--pre-tool-use-unavailable noop` marker path is unchanged and stays match-all.
- The scoped `exec` policy expands to Codex's shell spellings (`Bash`, `exec_command`) so a registered policy can never be skipped by a name mismatch; over-covering only costs a spawn.
- Scoped trusted hashes fold the matcher into the identity exactly as Codex's normalized `MatcherGroup` serializes.

## User Impact

Operators whose plugins scope their tool hooks (e.g. a hook that only guards the `message` tool) go from "relay spawn on every tool call" to "relay spawn on matching calls only" — near-zero relay spawns for typical shell-heavy Codex turns, with no loss of policy coverage. No config surface added; plugin authors opt in with one optional field.

## Evidence

Local proof (remote Testbox backend unavailable in this environment — `crabbox` binary failed sanity checks, so trusted-source gates ran locally per repo policy):

- Focused tests (all green): `src/plugins/tool-hook-matcher.test.ts` (11), `src/plugins/trusted-tool-policy.test.ts` (6), `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware.test.ts` (7), `src/plugins/hooks.before-tool-call.test.ts` (13, incl. matcher dispatch/short-circuit), `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (89, incl. 4 new tool-scope tests), `src/agents/harness/tool-result-middleware.test.ts` (25), `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.approval-binding.test.ts` (2), `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (19, incl. matcher config + trust-hash divergence + no-op match-all + exact-safety fallback tests)
- Typecheck: `tsgo` core / extensions / core-test / extensions-test / test-root all clean
- `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on changed files: clean; `git diff --check`: clean
- `pnpm check:import-cycles`: 0 cycles
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: within budget (no new SDK exports; the scope type is reachable via `NativeHookRelayRegistrationHandle["toolScopeForEvent"]`)
- `pnpm build`: green, no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`

target.title: feat: ask_user — structured questions from the agent with web card, channel buttons, and text answers
target.body:
Related: #109724 (Codex-parity slice 1: this PR is the provider-neutral question RPC that PR deliberately deferred)

## What Problem This Solves

Agents had no first-class way to ask the human a structured question and wait for the answer. The embedded agent could only guess or write prose questions into chat; Codex harness questions got a text-only prompt on channels; and there was no provider-neutral pause/prompt/resume primitive that web UI and message channels could share (the pattern Claude Code ships as `AskUserQuestion` and Codex ships as `request_user_input`).

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the provider-neutral question runtime deferred by #109724, modeled on the existing exec-approval subsystem (the established blocking pause→prompt→resume template):

- **Gateway question runtime**: transient in-memory `question.request` / `question.waitAnswer` / `question.resolve` / `question.get` / `question.list` RPCs plus `question.requested` / `question.resolved` broadcasts under a new `operator.questions` scope (additive; no protocol version bump). Answers are validated against the stored record (unknown ids, cardinality, option membership) and canonicalized before terminalizing; `isSecret` and duplicate option labels are rejected at the request boundary.
- **`ask_user` tool** for the embedded agent (main sessions only, not subagents): 1–3 questions, 2–4 options each (labels ≤64 chars), `multiSelect`, free-text "Other" always available, recommended-option-first convention, `timeoutSeconds` 30–3600 (default 900). The tool blocks like exec approvals; expiry returns a `no_answer` result telling the model to proceed with best judgment.
- **Chat delivery**: the question is delivered to the originating conversation while the tool blocks — as a `MessagePresentation` with native tap-to-answer buttons via a new runtime-authored `{type:"question"}` presentation action (Telegram inline keyboards `tgq1:` ≤64 bytes, Discord custom ids `ocq` ≤100 chars, Slack Block Kit `slq1:`), degrading to numbered text on button-less channels. A plain text reply (number, label, or free text) answers on any channel; the reply is consumed as the answer instead of steering into the run.
- **Control UI**: one unified in-thread question card serving both gateway `ask_user` questions (broadcast-driven, click/multi-select/free-text, resolve over the gateway, terminal states incl. answered-elsewhere/expired) and the existing Codex stream questions from #109724 (composer submit path unchanged).

Codex upstream contract checked directly at `openai/codex@9ff47868eb`: `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/request_user_input.rs`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1585-1637` (schema conventions: header ≤12 chars, recommended-first, forced free-text "Other", root-thread-only — mirrored here). Converging the Codex/Copilot harness bridges onto this runtime is a named follow-up, not part of this PR.

## User Impact

Agents can now pause and ask a real question with buttons. Users answer by clicking in the web Control UI, tapping a native button on Telegram/Discord/Slack, or just replying in text on any channel; the agent resumes with structured answers. Docs: `docs/tools/ask-user.md`.

Pending card (web):
![pending](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/01-question-pending.png)
Answered:
![answered](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/02-question-answered.png)
MultiSelect:
![multiselect](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/03-question-multiselect.png)
Terminal states (answered elsewhere / expired):
![terminal](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/04-question-terminal-states.png)

## Evidence

- **Live end-to-end proof** on a source-checkout gateway (isolated `--dev` state dir, `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`): agent called `ask_user` with a single-select + multiSelect pair, blocked 1m03s, the web card rendered in-thread, options were clicked (Staging + Integration/E2E), the gateway resolved, and the agent resumed enumerating exactly those answers. This live run also caught and fixed a gating bug (`isEmbeddedMode()` is the TUI-host flag, not the embedded-runner flag — `ask_user` was invisible to normal gateway runs until commit `ce0251e6bb9`'s fix).
- **Playwright e2e** `ui/src/e2e/question-flow.e2e.test.ts` (3 tests, mock gateway): render → resolve payload shape (`{answers:{deploy_target:{answers:["Staging (Recommended)"]}}}`) → resolved state; multiSelect arrays; answered-elsewhere + expired terminal states. Screenshots above are its artifacts.
- **Focused suites** (local, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`): gateway question manager + RPC handlers + protocol validators, ask_user tool (normalize/execute/claim/abort races), subscriber delivery, outbound presentation precedence, per-channel envelope round-trips incl. byte limits, UI prompt state machine + card + thread placement — all green (500+ tests across the touched files).
- **Typecheck/lint**: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, targeted oxlint — green (Testbox + local fallback when Testbox returned 429).
- **Build**: full `pnpm build` green, no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`.
- **Autoreview** (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh): three iterations; 7 findings accepted and fixed (answer validation at resolve, isSecret fail-closed, duplicate-label rejection, UI retry latch, reconnect `QUESTION_NOT_FOUND` terminalization, option-label bound, answer canonicalization); final run clean — "no accepted/actionable findings".

Follow-ups (intentionally out of scope): converge Codex/Copilot harness user-input bridges onto the question runtime; reaction-based answering on WhatsApp/Signal/iMessage; unbind channel buttons after resolution; MCP elicitation routing (pending the 2026-07-28 MRTR spec).

target.title: fix(ai): guard stream error serialization against circular non-Error values (issues #106570 #106568)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The OpenAI Completions and Google stream error handlers serialize non-Error exceptions with `JSON.stringify(error)`. When the error is a network error carrying circular socket references, `JSON.stringify` throws a `TypeError`, crashing the error handler and preventing the stream from closing gracefully — unhandled rejections, FD leaks, and hangs in downstream consumers during network outages.

This is the same crash at two sibling call sites (issues #106570 and #106568).

## Evidence

- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts:565` `error instanceof Error ? error.message : JSON.stringify(error)`
- `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts:469` identical line
- A circular non-Error (e.g. `{ code: "ECONNRESET", self }`) makes `JSON.stringify` throw, taking down the `catch` block that was supposed to emit the error.
- `scripts/proof-stream-error-serialize.mjs` reproduces it: OLD `JSON.stringify(circular)` throws; NEW guarded serialize returns `String(error)` without throwing.

## Fix

Wrap the non-Error branch in try/catch, falling back to `String(error)` on serialization failure. Applied identically at both call sites — one guard, same bug class, no new helper (the existing `src/utils/safe-json.ts` lives in the main `src` tree and is not importable from the `packages/ai` package boundary, so an inline guard avoids a cross-package export).

```text
$ node scripts/proof-stream-error-serialize.mjs
OLD JSON.stringify(circular) throws? true
NEW guarded serialize returns: "[object Object]"
NEW did not throw? true
RESULT: PASS — circular error no longer crashes the stream error handler
```

Closes #106570
See also #106568 (identical Google-provider crash, fixed by the same change)
## Runtime Proof

`scripts/proof-stream-error-serialize.mjs` mirrors the exact guarded serialization from
both call sites and runs a circular non-Error (network error with a self-reference):

```text
$ node scripts/proof-stream-error-serialize.mjs
OLD JSON.stringify(circular) throws? true
NEW guarded serialize returns: "[object Object]"
NEW did not throw? true

RESULT: PASS — circular error no longer crashes the stream error handler
```

The committed fix is also covered by the existing provider test setup where available;
the standalone script proves the guard without requiring live provider credentials.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

target.title: fix(ui): release Talk media after WebRTC disconnects
target.body:
[AI-assisted] ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Realtime Talk could leave microphone, camera, and audio resources active after an OpenAI WebRTC connection failed or closed unexpectedly. ## Why This Change Was Made Terminal peer connection failures now run the existing transport teardown after reporting the error. This keeps cleanup idempotent while releasing owned media streams, audio contexts, timers, data channels, and peer resources without requiring a manual stop action. ## User Impact Talk sessions now release browser media resources promptly when their provider connection ends unexpectedly, instead of keeping capture or playback resources alive until the user dismisses the session. ## Evidence
Before — origin/main After — PR head
- Real browser Before/After in Playwright Chromium 149.0.7827.55 with the same mocked OpenAI WebRTC failure: - Before (`origin/main` at `93e9e2fe935d83234144fb5105e2aa618f7c1fb1`): the error appeared, the camera preview remained visible, and both captured media tracks remained `live`. - After (PR head `97dad7f9af3da17f79b76698350d0922b7df622a`): the same error appeared, the camera preview was removed, and both captured media tracks changed to `ended`. - `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-webrtc-video.test.ts` — 1 file and 2 tests passed. The regression triggers a terminal peer connection failure and asserts error reporting plus microphone, camera, and audio teardown. - `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-webrtc.ts ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-webrtc-video.test.ts` — passed. - `pnpm tsgo:ui` — passed. - `pnpm --dir ui build` — passed. - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --stream-engine-output` — clean; no accepted or actionable findings.

## Summary

- Fail closed when Codex app-server thread items report an unrecognized non-empty status instead of projecting them as successful completions.

- Keep existing known status and known notification behavior unchanged; this only affects unknown protocol drift and ignored event diagnostics.

## Linked context

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where guarded HTTP redirects could leave an unread response body attached to the dispatcher when the redirect was rejected because of a missing or invalid `Location`, a loop, or the redirect limit. Repeated failures could delay connection reuse and retain transport resources.

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

Tools that may yield must declare `executionMode: "sequential"`. Agent-core inspects that declaration before starting the batch, so a successful yield aborts the turn before later sibling tools run. A yield result from a default/parallel tool is rejected before the runtime control handler is invoked. Sequential tools remain model-visible and are excluded from Tool Search, Code Mode, and headless catalogs because those outer bridges cannot preserve the target tool's pre-execution scheduling identity.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration; only tools that opt into yield must declare sequential execution.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.
- Require yielding tools to declare `executionMode: "sequential"` and reject incompatible results.
- Stop a sequential batch after yield so later side-effectful sibling tools never start.
- Keep sequential tools on the direct execution surface instead of hiding them behind Tool Search, Code Mode, or headless catalogs.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "id": "yield-proof",
    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },
  "finalizedResult": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"
    },
    "control": {
      "type": "yield",
      "message": "Waiting for proof card answer"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "sessionId": "proof-session-1",
    "yieldEvents": ["Waiting for proof card answer"],
    "yieldDetected": true,
    "modelCalls": 2,
    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },
      "isError": false
    },
    "resumedAssistant": {
      "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Answer accepted." }],
      "stopReason": "stop"
    }
  }
}
```

### Finalization, scheduling, and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are the values applied by the runtime.
- Agent-core tests prove an unsupported finalized control becomes an explicit tool error.
- Agent-core tests prove a non-sequential yielding tool is rejected before its control handler runs.
- Agent-core tests prove a sequential yielding tool prevents a later side-effectful sibling from starting.
- Catalog tests prove sequential tools remain direct across Tool Search and Code Mode and are omitted from headless catalogs.
- Embedded orchestration coverage proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

### Verification

- Scheduler TDD RED: CI run `29575710823` failed the new non-sequential-yield assertion before the guard existed.
- Scheduler TDD GREEN: the same Node shard passed in CI run `29576120720` after the guard was added.

target.title: Bound ChatGPT websocket Blob frame reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT WebSocket responses accept string, ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferView, and Blob-like frames. The Blob-like path previously called `arrayBuffer()` before checking any advertised frame size, so an oversized frame could force whole-frame materialization before the existing stream/body size caps had a chance to apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` now checks Blob-like `size` before calling `arrayBuffer()`. Frames larger than the existing ChatGPT Responses success-body cap fail with the existing WebSocket message-too-big close code instead of allocating the full body.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Blob-like WebSocket frame could be materialized in full even when it advertised a size above the provider's bounded response limit.

**After:** Oversized Blob-like WebSocket frames are rejected before `arrayBuffer()` is called. Normal string, ArrayBuffer, typed-array, and Blob-like frames within the cap keep the same decode behavior.

## Evidence

**Scope:** 1 file.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` (+13/-1): size check before Blob.arrayBuffer() call.

### Pre-submit checks: ✅ PASSED on Linux

target.title: Fix MSTeams card actions with durable receive before ACK
target.body:
## What problem this solves

Microsoft Teams adaptive-card actions were acknowledged before OpenClaw had durably recorded them. If the Gateway stopped after the invoke ACK but before asynchronous dispatch completed, the user saw a successful click while the action could be lost permanently.

## What changed

- Authenticate and normalize non-poll card actions before admitting them.
- Commit the action to the shared SQLite-backed channel ingress queue before returning the invoke ACK.
- Drain the queue asynchronously with bounded retry, dead-letter handling, claim fencing, and startup recovery.
- Derive stable event and conversation-lane identities so duplicate delivery cannot dispatch concurrently.
- Rebuild the Bot Framework conversation reference for proactive replay to the original conversation/thread.
- Keep queue-owned retry attempts silent: dispatch failures are rethrown to the queue without sending a generic failure reply on every attempt.

Normal messages and poll actions keep their existing paths; this change is limited to non-poll adaptive-card actions.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite lifecycle tests cover commit-before-return, restart recovery, bounded transient retry, post-adoption terminal handling, duplicate fencing, and correct conversation/thread replay.
- Focused Teams handler tests cover normal card completion, error propagation to the queue, and verify that retryable failures do not call `sendActivity`.
- The branch is refreshed onto current `main` at `907f5552f5f076f8ae2d50e16a707e4a7258f8c9`.
- [GitHub Actions CI run 29577503313](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29577503313) is green, including changed Node tests, production/test type checks, lint, dependency and package-boundary checks, build artifacts, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- The implementation was checked against the pinned `@microsoft/teams.apps` 2.0.13 invoke-response, proactive conversation, and activity-send contracts.

## Live Teams validation limitation

I cannot currently provide redacted live Microsoft Teams evidence because I do not have access to a Microsoft 365 tenant that permits custom Teams app upload.

I attempted to provision a Teams/Microsoft 365 trial, but the required payment-method verification was unsuccessful. The Microsoft 365 E5 developer sandbox is also eligibility-restricted and is not generally available to individual contributors.

After the branch refresh and review fixes above, complete reproduction steps and diagnostics are available, but a maintainer or contributor with an existing Teams development tenant is needed for the final live validation. I have requested maintainer-assisted validation in a PR comment.

Requested live scenarios:

1. Confirm the durable ingress record is committed before the invoke ACK.
2. Confirm a normal non-poll card action completes successfully.
3. Stop the Gateway after ACK and verify recovery after restart.
4. Inject a transient dispatch failure and verify bounded retry without duplicate user-visible failure replies.

target.title: fix(doctor): repair ALTER-appended operator approval schema instead of wedging startup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a hard startup wedge where `openclaw gateway` refuses to start and `openclaw doctor --fix` circularly reports "has a legacy operator approval schema; run openclaw doctor --fix to migrate it" — leaving the user with no working path. Hit in production on a macOS install whose state database predates the `resolution_ref` column.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fail-closed matcher in `openclaw-state-db-operator-approval-migration.ts` only accepted the exact canonical-position legacy DDL. A real shipped upgrade path added `resolution_ref` via `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` (see `ensureAdditiveStateColumns`), producing a tail-appended nullable column. That shape failed the exact match, the repair no-oped, and `assertCanonicalStateSchemaShape` threw the same message doctor tells you to fix with doctor.

Three fixes, all fail-closed:
1. The matcher now accepts exactly four enumerated shapes: canonical-position or ALTER-appended `resolution_ref`, each STRICT or non-STRICT. Arbitrary schema differences still refuse migration.
2. The copy filters rows that cannot satisfy the canonical `resolution_ref TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length = 43, charset)` constraint (pre-ref rows hold NULL; non-STRICT tables can even hold BLOBs). Approvals are transient runtime state, so nonconforming rows are dropped rather than aborting the repair and re-wedging startup.
3. The table rebuild now replays only the operator-approval index statements instead of the entire canonical schema — executing the full schema mid-repair fails on many-versions-behind databases whose other tables still lack columns the later additive/STRICT repairs add ("no such column: agent_id").

Also: when the repair itself refuses or fails inside doctor, the warning no longer recursively recommends `doctor --fix`.

## User Impact

Users on older state databases can upgrade again: `openclaw doctor --fix` completes (verified against the affected production database: operator approvals migrated, 83 tables migrated to STRICT typing) and the gateway starts. No behavior change for canonical databases.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-state-db-operator-approval-migration.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts` — 85 tests pass (new coverage: ALTER-appended STRICT/non-STRICT repair, NULL/short/BLOB `resolution_ref` row filtering, fail-closed refusal of unrecognized shapes, non-circular doctor warning).
- `pnpm check:changed` gate clean (format, typechecks, lint, boundaries, database-first guards).
- Live proof: doctor --fix on the wedged production DB completed and the gateway now serves (previously hard-wedged).

target.title: fix: compaction usage guards and agent-loop turn correctness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a cluster of agent-loop and compaction correctness bugs:

- A stream that dies before its terminal usage event persists all-zero usage; that anchors the context-size estimate near zero, threshold auto-compaction silently stops firing, and later requests die on context overflow.
- Tool results without `content` inject `undefined` into the transcript and crash provider conversion on the next request, aborting the run with a malformed message persisted.
- Compaction budgets skipped context-visible entries (plugin-injected messages, branch summaries), so the keep-recent window was computed against the wrong token totals and cut points could not land on those boundaries.
- Compaction could produce empty summary entries when there was nothing to summarize.
- A *successful* response with high token usage could be misclassified as silent overflow, popping the completed assistant message and burning the one-shot overflow-recovery flag.
- A threshold compaction that ran just before delivering a queued user prompt resumed the loop first, so the model answered the compaction summary unprompted.
- Follow-ups queued by handlers reacting to the run ending were never delivered.
- Mid-run system-prompt/tool/model changes did not apply to the next turn on the session path (the wrapper dropped the loop's per-turn refresh context). This is now an explicit `AgentOptions.prepareNextTurnWithContext` API (additive; baseline regenerated via the sanctioned workflow).
- `dispose()` left retry/compaction/branch-summary/bash/agent work running.
- Settings reload did not resync steering/follow-up queue modes; after-tool-call overrides dropped unknown result fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

These bugs compound in long sessions: broken usage accounting disables compaction exactly when it is most needed, and the loop-state gaps surface as duplicated or lost messages. The cut-point/turn-boundary logic is now expressed through one projection helper instead of parallel entry-type switches.

## User Impact

Long sessions keep compacting reliably; runs no longer crash on content-less tool results; queued messages are neither answered out of order nor dropped; mid-run model/prompt/tool changes take effect on the next turn; disposal is clean.

## Evidence

- 56 focused tests passing across `packages/agent-core` (agent-loop, compaction) and `src/agents/sessions` (context-usage, new loop-correctness suite with 10 cases), re-run after rebase onto current `main`.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` and `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (350 entrypoints; additive API only).
- Core + core-test typechecks and changed-file lint green (hosted run 29558685534).


**Live verification (real API keys):** `node scripts/test-live.mjs -- src/agents/sessions/agent-session.live.test.ts` — 3/3 against a real Claude model: a full agent turn with a registered tool executing end-to-end, **manual compaction of a small real session** (this PR's zero-retention replan producing a real model-generated summary, with the session remaining usable), and queued follow-up drain delivering a second answered message. Live suite added in this PR (gated on `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1` + key).

target.title: fix(onboard): keep configured AI route when guarded setup is skipped
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users rerunning guarded onboarding with an already configured AI route would be told to add AI later, and would never reach the hatch TUI, when they declined machine discovery and either skipped replacement setup or had no replacement choices. The manual stage returned `null` for both "keep the current route" and "continue without AI", and the caller treated both states as cancellation (`src/commands/onboard-guided.ts:596`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`listManualSetupInferenceOptions()` already owns the config-only classification and reports `setupComplete` when a default model is configured. The guided onboarding caller now carries that fact into the manual stage, preserves the existing route for both skip paths, and continues through the normal configured-install hatch handoff without rendering an empty applied summary.

## User Impact

Guarded users can decline discovery without losing the onboarding handoff for an AI route that is already configured. Fresh installs with no active route keep the existing cancellation and "add AI later" behavior.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Guarded onboarding preserves an already configured inference route when discovery is declined and no replacement route is selected or available.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, commit `f3fd29b47e43` on branch `fix/guarded-onboarding-keep-configured-route`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-guarded-route.mts` - writes an isolated configured-model state, executes the real guided onboarding entry point with guarded/manual selections and zero replacement choices, and records the hatch handoff.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live stdout):

  ```text
  PASS selections=guarded,manual keptRoute=true hatch=true
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The current route is retained, setup application is not invoked, and onboarding hands the configured workspace to the hatch TUI.
- **What was not tested:** A real provider turn and interactive terminal rendering were not exercised because the failure occurs before provider activation; the runtime proof uses the production onboarding flow with deterministic prompt and handoff adapters.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/onboard-guided.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       30 passed (30)

$ git diff --check
EXIT=0
```

The regression test failed before the source fix because `launchHatchTui` had zero calls. Coverage now includes both an explicit replacement skip and a configured route with zero manual/auth choices.

Structured Codex autoreview was attempted with `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output`, but the review transport returned HTTP 403 before a model response. The changed function, caller, config-only `setupComplete` producer, sibling active-route path, and adjacent tests were reviewed manually.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes - configured guarded reruns now continue to the hatch instead of exiting as AI-less.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config shape, default, persistence, or migration changes.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - the patch only changes control flow after config-only route classification.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No - no provider activation contract or plugin surface changes.
- Highest-risk area: Distinguishing a deliberate AI-less skip from retaining a previously configured route.
- Mitigation: The existing `setupComplete` contract is used as the discriminator, with separate regressions for skip and empty-choice paths plus a direct runtime proof.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

target.title: improve: let Code Mode use declared tool result shapes
target.body:
Related: #109288
Follow-up to #109651 and #109290

AI-assisted: Yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode learned exact tool ids and compact input signatures from #109651, but every tool result still appeared as unknown. Even when a tool had a stable structured result, models often spent one exec returning the raw value and another exec processing fields they could have known up front. This left avoidable model turns, tokens, and latency in common multi-operation workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trusted OpenClaw core and plugin tools can now declare an optional `outputSchema` for `AgentToolResult.details`. Code Mode and Tool Search expose a bounded TypeScript-style output hint only when that schema is complete and closed; open, oversized, unsupported, MCP, and client schemas remain unknown and raw-first.

OpenClaw compiles trusted output schemas before execution, then validates final details after normal hooks. Framework-owned pre-execution policy blocks remain outside the success schema and are recognized by object identity, so calls reject with the denial reason before generated code can treat a block as a successful value; tool-authored blocked lookalikes still fail validation. Runtime/provider normalization preserves the result contract when it clones tool definitions. The compact renderer has strict depth/property/character/union bounds and normalizes AJV-style nullable schemas so every validator-accepted `null` remains visible to generated code. Remote and client schemas stay deferred as `input: "unknown"` and use object identity for catalog reuse, preventing attacker-sized metadata walks while preserving schema-replacement invalidation. `agents_list` adopts the contract as the first built-in example.

The change also promotes Code Mode to a dedicated `/tools/code-mode` documentation page with Quickstart, runtime semantics, guest API, output-contract authoring, trust/validation rules, fallback behavior, debugging, and validation guidance. The old `/reference/code-mode` route redirects to it.

## Maintainer Decision

Approve `outputSchema` as the supported optional plugin API for describing and validating `AgentToolResult.details` across Code Mode and Tool Search. Tools that omit it retain existing behavior. Opted-in tools get pre-execution schema compilation, final-details validation, and framework-owned policy-result preservation.

## User Impact

Code Mode can call and process tools with declared result shapes in the first exec instead of paying a raw-inspection round trip. Unknown outputs keep the safe existing raw-first behavior. Plugin authors get one documented result contract shared by Tool Search and Code Mode, without trusting remote MCP or client schema claims.

## Evidence

Live multi-provider matrix: four validated Code Mode tasks per provider over the real Agent runtime and a 72-tool catalog with adversarial decoys. Baseline is merged #109651; after is this branch.

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Validated tasks | 11/12 | 12/12 | +1 |
| Model turns | 29 | 26 | -10% |
| Code Mode exec calls | 17 | 14 | -18% |
| Decoy calls | 0 | 0 | unchanged |
| Total latency | 81.4s | 70.4s | -13% |
| Input tokens | 38,827 | 36,025 | -7% |
| Output tokens | 2,388 | 2,380 | unchanged |

Stress: three complete Code Mode matrices produced 34/36 validated tasks, 78 turns, 42 exec calls, 57 underlying service calls, and zero decoy calls. Anthropic and Google were 12/12; OpenAI was 10/12. Both misses were the model filtering singular fixture value `plum` with the plural word `plums` after selecting the correct real tool, not a discovery, transport, schema, or decoy failure. A final OpenAI/Google pass kept every completed task at two turns and one exec. The final Anthropic retry hit provider overload before tokens or tools; earlier Anthropic stress was 12/12.

Validation:

- Exact final head: 272 focused tests passed across the live-bench parser, Code Mode, Tool Search, runtime normalization, schema hints, `agents_list`, plugin SDK, descriptor cache, and optional tool metadata.
- Blacksmith Testbox on the earlier pre-review head: 254 focused tests passed; all changed gates passed, including core/plugin/test/script typechecks, full lint, SDK API/surface/boundary checks, and the full production build. Later contract fixes passed their exact-head focused suites locally and receive fresh hosted CI before merge.
- Adversarial regressions cover malformed schemas before side effects, post-hook result validation, policy-block rejection with preserved reason, blocked-lookalike rejection, nullable scalar/object contracts, cloned runtime tools retaining hints and validation, schema replacement, closed/truncated/unsupported shapes, huge keys/catalogs, untrusted client/MCP schema deferral, and zero traversal of hostile schema proxies.
- Source-blind behavior contract: satisfied at 0.86 confidence; all seven clauses passed, including state-changing irrigation, missing-tool recovery, zero decoys, provider-error classification, and docs navigation/redirect behavior.
- Autoreview: clean on the runtime-normalization fix at 0.97 confidence, policy-block contract fix at 0.95, and nullable-contract fix at 0.94. target.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening
target.body:
# PR Title

`feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening`

---

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's gateway already validates browser `Origin` on the WebSocket path, but only **post-handshake** (in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-admission.ts`, after the socket is already open), and it does **not** defend against:

- **Header-smuggling / contradiction attacks** — a client forging `X-Forwarded-For` to disagree with `Forwarded` (or vice-versa) to confuse the resolved client IP / trust decision.
- **Cross-site WebSocket initiations (CSRF / DNS-rebinding class)** — there is no `Sec-Fetch-Site` gate anywhere in `main` (`git grep` confirms zero `sec-fetch-site` enforcement in `src/`).
- **Proto contradiction** — `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `Forwarded proto` disagreeing with the actual socket transport (without breaking legitimate TLS-terminating trusted proxies).

These gaps are the WebSocket sibling of the now-closed HTTP ingress CSRF findings **#102834** and **#96486**, and sit *under* the origin-allowlist work in **#98924** (which decides *which* origins pass, not *when/how the gate runs*).

This PR adds a self-contained **pre-handshake** `verifyClient` gate attached to the gateway `WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })`, so unauthenticated or forged clients never complete the HTTP 101 upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Pre-handshake beats post-handshake.** Running the checks in `verifyClient` (before the 101) means a rejected client never gets a live socket, matching the defense-in-depth posture maintainers expect for a network-exposed gateway.
- **Reuses the shared `checkBrowserOrigin`** rather than reinventing origin logic, so allowlist / same-host / loopback behavior stays consistent with the HTTP/WS admission paths.
- **All strictness is opt-in and default-off** (`gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation`, `rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders`, `rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests`), so existing deployments have **zero behavior change**. Non-browser clients (CLI, native apps) send no `Origin` and pass through; they authenticate post-handshake as today.
- **Trusted proxies are correctly exempted** from the proto-mismatch check — a TLS-terminating proxy legitimately presents plaintext to the gateway.

This is complementary to **#98924** (`allowedOriginPatterns`): that PR extends *which* loopback origins are allowed; this PR adds the *enforcement layer* (pre-handshake gate, header contradiction, `Sec-Fetch-Site`). Neither duplicates the other.

## Prior Attempt & What Improved

This is a follow-up to my earlier (closed) PR **#35109** (`fix(gateway): surgical proxy-aware origin validation`), which edited the shared `checkBrowserOrigin` on the *post-handshake* WS path. Compared to that attempt, this PR:

- Moves the gate to **pre-handshake** (`verifyClient` before the 101) instead of extending the post-handshake check — a rejected client never opens a socket.
- Adds the **`Sec-Fetch-Site` cross-site rejection** and **`X-Forwarded-For` vs `Forwarded` IP-contradiction** checks that #35109 did not cover.
- Keeps the change **self-contained** in `verify-client.ts` + `forwarded-headers.ts` rather than widening the shared `checkBrowserOrigin` contract used by every HTTP/WS caller.
- Ran the `autoreview` closeout gate before opening; it caught a real **`Origin: null` bypass** (a literal `null` origin was treated like an absent header and skipped all browser validation). Fixed in `verify-client.ts` with a regression test — the gate now only fast-passes on a *truly absent* Origin.

The goal was to take the earlier direction, make it architecturally cleaner, and actually vet it before asking for review.

## User Impact

- Network-exposed gateways gain a pre-handshake defense against forged forwarded headers and cross-site WebSocket CSRF, with **no config change required** for existing users (all new behavior opt-in).
- Operators who want stricter posture can enable:
  - `gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation` — reject duplicate / comma-chained sensitive proxy headers.
  - `gateway.security.rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders` — reject proxy headers from non-trusted peers.
  - `gateway.security.rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests` — reject `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` / `cross-origin` WebSocket upgrades. **Off by default**; opt in only when every legitimate browser WS client is same-origin to the gateway. Loopback aliases (e.g. `localhost` -> `127.0.0.1`) are legitimately flagged cross-site by browsers, so the gate stays opt-in and `checkBrowserOrigin` remains authoritative.

## Evidence

Real gateway/WS behavior, driven through the actual `verify-client` factory (not mocked):

```
# Trusted proxy presenting plaintext X-Forwarded-Proto -> ACCEPTED (proto-mismatch exempt)
remote=127.0.0.1  origin=https://app.example.com  x-forwarded-proto=https  -> ok=true

# Identical request from an UNTRUSTED peer -> REJECTED
remote=198.51.100.7  origin=https://app.example.com  x-forwarded-proto=https  -> ok=false

# Cross-site WebSocket initiation from a browser -> REJECTED (Sec-Fetch-Site)
remote=192.0.2.10  origin=https://evil.example.com  sec-fetch-site=cross-site -> ok=false

# Literal "null" browser origin -> REJECTED (no longer skips the gate)
remote=192.0.2.10  origin=null  sec-fetch-site=cross-site -> ok=false

# Non-browser client with no Origin header -> PASSES THROUGH
remote=192.0.2.10  (no Origin)  -> ok=true
```

- Test file: `src/gateway/server/verify-client.test.ts` — **5/5 passing** (trusted-proxy wiring regression, untrusted-peer reject, cross-site reject, `Origin: null` reject, non-browser pass-through). The trusted-proxy case guards a real prior regression where `gateway.trustedProxies` was never read at the call site.
- `tsgo` typecheck: **clean** on both `verify-client.ts` and `forwarded-headers.ts`.
- `autoreview` (Codex, high reasoning): initially reported the `Origin: null` bypass; after the fix, no accepted/actionable findings.

## Scope / Out of scope

- **In scope:** `src/gateway/server/verify-client.ts` (new, wired at `server-runtime-state.ts`), `src/gateway/forwarded-headers.ts` (validators), their tests, and the `gateway.security.*` config surface in `src/config/types.gateway.ts` + `src/config/zod-schema.ts`.
- **Out of scope (left to maintainer decision):** the `#98924` allowlist-wildcard contract, and the broader `gateway.browserOrigins` client/role-scoped policy direction.
- **`Sec-Fetch-Site` note for reviewers:** upstream deliberately avoids a blanket `cross-site` reject on MCP **HTTP** because browsers flag legit local MCP as cross-site. This PR mirrors that posture for the **WebSocket upgrade** path: the reject is **opt-in** (`gateway.security.rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests: true`) and runs *after* `checkBrowserOrigin`, so the existing origin allowlist / loopback-alias admission (shipped in v2026.4.15, PR #66665) remains authoritative. Native/CLI clients send no `Sec-Fetch-Site` header so they pass through regardless.

## Related

- Sibling enforcement: **#98924** (`allowedOriginPatterns`, open) — which origins are allowed.
- Prior art (closed security findings this complements): **#102834** (HTTP ingress CSRF under `auth.mode=none`), **#96486** (CSRF via the existing `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback`, which this PR reuses verbatim rather than duplicating).
- Prior attempt by me: **#35109** (closed) — see "Prior Attempt & What Improved".

cc @steipete — this sits on the gateway origin/security boundary you own (and is the sibling of #98924 / the closed #102834, #96486). The `Sec-Fetch-Site` reject is scoped to the WS upgrade pre-handshake specifically because of the MCP-HTTP caveat you handled; happy to align flag names / gate position with #98924 before merge if you'd prefer.


---

## ClawSweeper Follow-up (head `1b5c1de`)

Addressed all four findings from the July 17 ClawSweeper review in a single follow-up commit (`1b5c1de7ed5`):

1. **[P1] Default-on Sec-Fetch-Site reject → opt-in.** `rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests` now defaults to `false` (`=== true` instead of `!== false`), matching this PR's stated "all flags default-off" design and preserving the v2026.4.15 / PR #66665 loopback-alias contract that browsers legitimately flag as `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`. Regression test added (`allows legitimate loopback cross-site traffic by default`).
2. **[P1] Duplicate config field removed.** `gateway.security.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` is gone; `verify-client` now reads the existing `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` so pre-handshake and post-handshake admission share one source of truth.
3. **[P2] Canonical IPv6 parsing.** `forwarded-headers.ts` now uses `normalizeIpAddress` from `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` instead of `split(":")[0]`. Bracketed / unbracketed / port-suffixed IPv6 literals all normalize correctly. Regression tests added for IPv6 contradiction detection and matching-across-forms.
4. **[P2] Public config contract completed.** `gateway.security` plus its three leaf fields now have entries in `schema.labels.ts`, `schema.tags.ts`, and `schema.help.ts` (all ≥80 chars with operational guidance, per `schema.help.quality.test.ts`).

Net diff: +50/-40 prod LOC across 8 files. The PR got smaller, not larger. All unit tests (`verify-client`: 8/8, `schema.help.quality`: 22/22) and `tsgo` core typecheck are green on the new head.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): redact credential-shaped text in embedding API errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The GitHub Copilot embeddings integration echoes credential-shaped text into user-visible error diagnostics. Both non-2xx paths — model discovery (`discoverEmbeddingModels`) and the embeddings call itself (`createGitHubCopilotEmbeddingProvider`) — send a Copilot bearer token to a configurable base URL, then interpolate the bounded upstream response body verbatim into the thrown `Error`. If an upstream or proxy response reflected token-shaped or credential-shaped data, that content surfaced unredacted in error messages, logs, and any operator-facing diagnostics for the Copilot embeddings provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both error paths now wrap the bounded response body read with `redactSensitiveText(..., { mode: "tools" })` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core` before interpolation.

The explicit `{ mode: "tools" }` is the important part: these errors are a credential-safety boundary, so masking must not inherit the operator's general logging preference. Called without options, `redactSensitiveText` resolves `logging.redactSensitive` and returns the input unchanged when that setting is `off` (see `src/logging/redact.ts`), which would defeat the fix. Forcing `tools` mode keeps the reflected body masked regardless of that setting.

This reuses the established in-boundary SDK redaction helper (already used elsewhere in the tree) and the existing `readResponseTextLimited` reader, so no new dependency, abstraction, or boundary crossing is introduced. The existing 8 KiB streaming read bound (`COPILOT_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`) is preserved, and the exact error message prefixes are unchanged (`GitHub Copilot model discovery HTTP <status>:` and `GitHub Copilot embeddings HTTP <status>:`). Preserving those prefixes matters because `isCopilotSetupError` matches on them for auto-selection fallback. Only the interpolated body segment is redacted; status codes and safe reason text are retained.

This addresses the ClawSweeper P1 finding "Force redaction independently of logging settings" and its recommended maintainer option "Force boundary redaction before merge".

## User Impact

- Before: with a reflected credential in an upstream/proxy body, a Copilot embeddings failure could surface the raw token in the thrown error and logs. With `logging.redactSensitive: off`, even the prior redaction attempt would have passed the raw body through unchanged.
- After: the reflected body segment is masked at both error boundaries regardless of `logging.redactSensitive`, while the HTTP status and human-readable failure reason are preserved. No change to success paths, error message prefixes, Copilot setup detection, or auto-selection fallback.

## Evidence

**Scope:** 2 files.
- `extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.ts` (+16/-2): force-redaction at both non-2xx error boundaries.
- `extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.transport.test.ts` (+238, new): real-transport regression proof.

### Regression test

`extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.transport.test.ts` drives the production adapter (`githubCopilotMemoryEmbeddingProviderAdapter`) against a loopback `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0`. It does **not** mock `fetch`, `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime`, or `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core` (`redactSensitiveText` is exercised end to end). Only auth/token resolution uses synthetic fixtures. Four cases:

1. **Model discovery error (401)** — server body contains `ghu_...`; asserts the thrown error keeps `HTTP 401` and `authentication failed` but does NOT contain the full token or its `UNIQUESECRET` component.
2. **Embeddings error (429)** — server body contains `gho_...`; asserts `HTTP 429` and `rate limit exceeded` preserved, token and `UNIQUEEMBSECRET` component absent.
3. **Redaction disabled in config (403)** — writes an on-disk config with `logging.redactSensitive: "off"` (via `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`), then asserts the `ghu_...` token is still masked. This is the guard for the forced-`tools`-mode boundary: a config-honoring call would leak the token here.
4. **Success path (200)** — asserts a valid embeddings response still returns a numeric vector of the expected length, proving no behavior change on the happy path.

### Pre-submit checks: ✅ PASSED on Linux

All checks validated on Linux checkout:

```bash
$ oxfmt --check extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.ts extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.transport.test.ts
Checking formatting...
All matched files use the correct format.
Finished in 80ms on 2 files using 8 threads.

# No errors, passed cleanly

$ pnpm test extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.transport.test.ts

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 10.84s

   Start at  19:02:21
   Duration  5.34s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 10.24s

$ $autoreview
# No findings, exit code 0
```

### Notes

- Verified against live `openclaw/openclaw` `main`: both error paths still read the response body raw with no redaction, so this change is not superseded.
- Branch rebased onto latest `main`; `extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.test.ts` is unchanged from `main` (the earlier oxfmt failure on that file no longer applies).

target.title: test(macos): anchor chat fixture timestamps to send-time events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two macOS Swift Testing flakes failed the macos-swift lane on main (run 29573675642): `ChatHapticsTests` "durable assistant failure fires run failed" (both parameterized cases) and `ChatStreamReplayTests` "reconnect mid-run converges via history refetch" — all "Timeout waiting for" failures at ~17s.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared mechanism, not two: fixture timestamps were anchored to wall clock at **test start**, raced against the optimistic user-echo timestamp captured later at **send time**. The only pending-run drain these fake transports have is `clearPendingRunIfAssistantMessagePresent` → `assistantHapticEvent(after:)`, which requires the assistant row's timestamp ≥ the echo timestamp. Under `swift test --parallel` all suites share the MainActor; a >1s starvation between fixture creation and `send()` leaves the fixture row permanently "older" than the echo, so the drain can never fire — both parameterized cases fail together, exactly the CI signature. (The reconnect test also can't drain via the foreground refetch: its scripted history has no `inFlightRun`, so only the timestamp comparison exists.)

Fix is event-ordered anchoring, no margins, no timeout changes:
- Haptics: the fake transport takes a history closure evaluated per `requestHistory`, stamping the failure row at fetch time — which is strictly after the echo append, so ordering holds by construction.
- Reconnect: the transcript anchors to a timestamp captured after the send completed.

## User Impact

None — test-only (mac app test fixtures).

## Evidence

- Deterministic repro: injecting a 1.5s / 1.2s stall before send reproduced both CI failures byte-for-byte; the fixes pass **with the stalls still injected** (proving immunity to scheduling delay), then stalls removed.
- Stress: 10/10 green runs of both tests; both full suites (10 tests) green.
- swiftformat --lint on both files: only a pre-existing docComments finding present at HEAD (Tests dirs aren't in CI lint lanes).
- Autoreview (codex/gpt-5.6-sol): clean, 0 findings, "patch is correct (0.94)".

target.title: Fix MSTeams card actions with durable receive before ACK
target.body:
## What problem this solves

Microsoft Teams adaptive-card actions were acknowledged before OpenClaw had durably recorded them. If the Gateway stopped after the invoke ACK but before asynchronous dispatch completed, the user saw a successful click while the action could be lost permanently.

## What changed

- Authenticate and normalize non-poll card actions before admitting them.
- Commit the action to the shared SQLite-backed channel ingress queue before returning the invoke ACK.
- Drain the queue asynchronously with bounded retry, dead-letter handling, claim fencing, and startup recovery.
- Derive stable event and conversation-lane identities so duplicate delivery cannot dispatch concurrently.
- Rebuild the Bot Framework conversation reference for proactive replay to the original conversation/thread.
- Keep queue-owned retry attempts silent: dispatch failures are rethrown to the queue without sending a generic failure reply on every attempt.

Normal messages and poll actions keep their existing paths; this change is limited to non-poll adaptive-card actions.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite lifecycle tests cover commit-before-return, restart recovery, bounded transient retry, post-adoption terminal handling, duplicate fencing, and correct conversation/thread replay.
- Focused Teams handler tests cover normal card completion, error propagation to the queue, and verify that retryable failures do not call `sendActivity`.
- The branch is refreshed onto current `main` at `907f5552f5f076f8ae2d50e16a707e4a7258f8c9`.
- [GitHub Actions CI run 29577503313](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29577503313) is green, including changed Node tests, production/test type checks, lint, dependency and package-boundary checks, build artifacts, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- The implementation was checked against the pinned `@microsoft/teams.apps` 2.0.13 invoke-response, proactive conversation, and activity-send contracts.

## Live Teams validation limitation

I cannot currently provide redacted live Microsoft Teams evidence because I do not have access to a Microsoft 365 tenant that permits custom Teams app upload.

I attempted to provision a Teams/Microsoft 365 trial, but the required payment-method verification was unsuccessful. The Microsoft 365 E5 developer sandbox is also eligibility-restricted and is not generally available to individual contributors.

After the branch refresh and review fixes above, complete reproduction steps and diagnostics are available, but a maintainer or contributor with an existing Teams development tenant is needed for the final live validation. I have requested maintainer-assisted validation in a PR comment.

Requested live scenarios:

1. Confirm the durable ingress record is committed before the invoke ACK.
2. Confirm a normal non-poll card action completes successfully.
3. Stop the Gateway after ACK and verify recovery after restart.
4. Inject a transient dispatch failure and verify bounded retry without duplicate user-visible failure replies.
5. Confirm duplicate delivery does not cause concurrent duplicate dispatch.
6. Confirm the proactive reply targets the correct conversation/thread.

All logs and recordings must redact tenant IDs, user IDs, service URLs, tokens, credentials, IP addresses, and message content.

target.title: [Bug]: OpenClaw v7.1 Dashboard Returns 400 Error with llamacpp due to Missing Regex Anchors in Auto-Generated GBNF Schema
target.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw v7.1 Dashboard returns a 400 Bad Request error when interacting with a local llamacpp provider due to missing ^ and $ anchors in the auto-generated GBNF schema, while the exact same agent and model work perfectly through a standard Gateway message channel.

### Steps to reproduce

Configure OpenClaw v7.1 to use a local llamacpp provider (e.g., Qwen3.6-27B-UDiq3).
Open the native OpenClaw Web Dashboard and send a message that triggers a tool call or requires schema validation.
Observe that the request fails with a 400 error.
In the exact same session, send a message through a custom WebUI that uses the standard Gateway message routing (_send_to_gateway('main', text)).
Observe that the request succeeds with a 200 OK response.

### Expected behavior

In previous versions (and currently via the standard Gateway message channel), both the native Dashboard and external clients successfully communicate with the llamacpp provider without schema validation errors.

### Actual behavior

The native Dashboard fails with a 400 error. The attached gateway log shows the exact error at 18:21:55 UTC: 400 Unable to generate parser for this template. Automatic parser generation failed: JSON schema conversion failed: Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'. The llamacpp provider strictly rejects the malformed pattern, while the custom WebUI processes the request successfully.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1

### Operating system

windows11

### Install method

_No response_

### Model

llamacpp/*

### Provider / routing chain

llamacpp with openai-completions

target.title: fix(ui): derive live cron and skill counts for Simple Automations card
target.body:
## Summary

The Quick Settings Automation card hardcoded cronJobCount and skillCount to 0, always displaying misleading zero counts regardless of real Gateway state. skillCount is now derived from config (same pattern as existing mcpServerCount), and cronJobCount is fetched once via gateway cron.status RPC on entry.

- Problem: Control UI Settings → Simple → Automations always showed "0 scheduled tasks" and "0 skills installed" even when the Gateway had real Cron jobs and Skills installed, because both values were hardcoded to 0.
- Solution: skillCount reads from config.skills.entries (config-driven, no RPC), cronJobCount fetches once via cron.status RPC when entering quick settings mode, with null-to-zero fallback until data arrives.
- What changed: `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts` (+40/-3): added skillCount() helper, added cronJobCount state with one-shot loadCronStatus() RPC loader, wired counts into renderQuickConfig(). `ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts` (+37/0): added tests for non-zero counts and singular label rendering.
- What did NOT change: MCP server count (remains config-derived via mcpServerCount), polling behavior (no periodic cron.status calls), i18n keys, UI layout, channels/security/appearance quick settings.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The "preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs" test uses a key `"abcdefg😀hijklmnop"` where the emoji sits at code-unit positions 7-8. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` would capture only the high surrogate; `truncateUtf16Safe` backs up to position 7, dropping the emoji entirely rather than outputting a broken half-character.

**What was not tested**: No UI-level integration test. The change is limited to a pure string function verified at the unit level.

## Tests and validation

- 7/7 tests passed in `live-test-helpers.test.ts` including emoji boundary preservation test

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low
"

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Claude Code CLI turns did not emit trusted `model.call.started`, `model.call.completed`, and `model.call.error` diagnostics. Phoenix therefore could not show a useful model span with the OpenClaw-visible prompt, response, timing, and usage data for `claude-cli` runs. ## Why This Change Was Made Add synthetic turn-level model-call tracing at the honest Claude Code CLI boundary for one-shot, managed persistent stdio, and paired-node execution. Each admitted attempt now receives exactly one terminal lifecycle event, including retry attempts, aborts, timeouts, process/parse failures, deferred background completion, persistence failure, and cleanup failure. Content capture reuses the existing trusted capture policy and remains disabled by default. Granular capture includes only the effective OpenClaw prompt, OpenClaw-appended system prompt, and visible assistant blocks. It intentionally excludes Claude Code private prompts, hidden resume/compaction payloads, native tool schemas and arguments, raw Anthropic HTTP traffic, internal retries, upstream request IDs, and network TTFB. Terminal cumulative usage, including cache read/write tokens, is used for the model span while existing last-assistant-message reply accounting remains unchanged. ## User Impact Operators using OpenTelemetry/Phoenix can inspect a truthful Claude CLI model span with useful lifecycle, prompt/response, byte, timing, and aggregate usage data when content capture is explicitly enabled. Default installations remain metadata-only, and native OpenClaw/Codex tracing behavior is unchanged. AI-assisted: yes (Codex). target.title: fix(agents): strip trailing assistant messages after sessions_yield artifact removal
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109638.

After `sessions_yield`, `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` removes aborted assistant messages and yield interrupt custom messages, but leaves trailing regular assistant messages (from pre-yield tool work) intact. When a sub-agent completes and auto-announce tries to inject a continuation message, it fails because the last visible message is an assistant — causing a deadlock.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.sessions-yield.ts`**: Added a second while-loop pass in `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` that strips any trailing regular assistant messages remaining after the yield-specific artifacts are removed. Updated `removeTrailingEntries` predicate to match.
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`**: Added regression test verifying that after stripping a transcript with pre-yield tool work, the last message is a `tool_result` (not an assistant).

## Why this is safe

`stripSessionsYieldArtifacts` is only called inside the yield abort handler (after `waitForSessionsYieldAbortSettle`). It never runs on non-yield sessions. Trailing assistant messages in the yield context are always intermediate tool-calling work — not meaningful final responses.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: After sessions_yield, auto-announce continuation delivery fails with role-continuity error because trailing assistant messages block injection.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.18.0, vitest

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts -t "trailing assistant" --reporter=verbose`

**Evidence after fix**: Test passes in both shards (agents-core 55ms, agents-embedded-agent 43ms). Last message after stripping is confirmed to be tool_result role.

**Observed result after fix**: 2 test files passed, 2 tests passed, 8 skipped (non-matching filter).

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end yield→announce flow (requires live sub-agent spawn + completion cycle, covered by integration environment).
